description: Comparison of token-overlap baseline vs semantic verification for previously missed SUPPORTED claims on the held-out test set.

claim_details.old_failure_reason: Jaccard token overlap was 0.4444 (below 0.70 support threshold). Evidence uses different wording: 'JSON configuration files' vs claim 'uses JSON for configuration'.
claim_details.new_decision_reason: Semantic similarity 0.9257 >= 0.72 threshold. No contradiction gates fired. Classified as SUPPORTED with high confidence.

claim_details.claim_text: sherpa repository files were last modified on 2026-10-31.
claim_details.old_failure_reason: Temporal mismatch: claim says '2026-10-31', evidence shows '31-10-2026' (different date format). Negation/polarity mismatch also triggered due to date format difference.
claim_details.new_decision_reason: Temporal mismatch gate still fires: claim date '2026-10-31' != evidence date '31-10-2026' (no overlap in extracted date patterns). Classified as CONTRADICTED despite high semantic similarity. This is a known limitation - date format normalization is not implemented.

claim_details.old_failure_reason: Jaccard overlap 0.2222 well below 0.70 threshold. Evidence lists multiple platforms, claim mentions only one.
claim_details.new_decision_reason: Semantic similarity 0.6636 is below 0.72 support threshold but above 0.55 partial threshold. Classified as PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED. The claim is fully supported by evidence but similarity falls just short of the SUPPORTED threshold.

claim_details.old_failure_reason: Jaccard overlap 0.2857 below 0.70 threshold. Compound claim split across two documents (D2, D3) not handled by token-overlap.
claim_details.new_decision_reason: Semantic similarity 0.7677 >= 0.72 but sub-claim coverage = 0.0 because sub-claim splitting on 'and' produced fragments that don't individually match evidence well. Falls to PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED due to coverage gate. Strong-match bypass (>=0.85) not triggered.

claim_details.new_decision_reason: Semantic similarity 0.4745 is below 0.55 partial threshold. The evidence text combines D6 and D8 content but the embedding model doesn't capture the cross-document reference well. Remains UNSUPPORTED.

claim_details.old_failure_reason: Jaccard overlap 0.6667 below 0.70 threshold but above 0.45 partial. Classified as PARTIAL.
claim_details.new_decision_reason: Semantic similarity 0.6377 below 0.72 support threshold. Compound claim coverage = 0.5 (one of two sub-claims supported). Classified as PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED.

claim_details.claim_text: sherpa has a templates directory and a workflows directory.
claim_details.old_failure_reason: Jaccard overlap 0.3636 below 0.70 threshold. Compound claim not handled.
claim_details.new_decision_reason: Semantic similarity 0.8713 >= 0.85 strong-match bypass threshold, BUT sub-claim coverage = 0.5 because splitting on 'and' creates fragments that don't individually match well. The strong-match bypass checks coverage first... actually coverage is 0.5 which is >= 0.25 partial threshold but < 0.70 support threshold. Since sim >= 0.85, strong-match bypass should trigger SUPPORTED. However, the current code checks contradiction first, then strong-match bypass. Let me verify: sim=0.8713 >= 0.85 → should be SUPPORTED. But prediction shows PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED. This indicates the strong-match bypass may not be working as expected for compound claims with coverage < support threshold.

Similarity just below 0.72 threshold for paraphrased claims (0.66-0.72 range)
Temporal/date format mismatch not normalized (e.g., '2026-10-31' vs '31-10-2026')
Multi-document evidence not handled well by single-text embedding comparison
